podcast.body: Produced by Rick Rubin, this album took about 18 months to complete, with an original release date in mid-2006 that was delayed. It was finally released on May 14, 2007, debuting at number one in 16 countries and eventually selling around 20 million copies worldwide. The band made a conscious decision to move away from pure new metal, with Mike Shinoda rapping on only two of 12 songs but singing lead on three others. "Minutes to Midnight came out on May 14, 2007, debuting at number one in 16 countries, and it would eventually sell somewhere around 20 million copies."

podcast.body: Released in 2007, this album sold 20 million copies. Its release followed a contentious contract renegotiation with Warner, which resulted in a $15 million advance and a high 20% royalty rate for the band, granting them greater creative control. "After that, minutes to midnight was released in 2007, and sold 20 million."

podcast.body: Released on May 15, 2007, this third studio album arrived more than four years after *Meteora* due to a contentious dispute with Warner Brothers Records. Super producer Rick Rubin was brought on board, and the album's creation involved 14 months of work spread over three years. It achieved the biggest opening week of any album in 2007, selling 625,000 copies in its first seven days and 3.3 million within the first month in the US. By year-end, it sold 4.3 million records, becoming the 7th best-selling record of 2007, with worldwide sales reaching about 6 million. "Studio album number three minutes to midnight did not come out until May 15th, 2007."
